FXUS65 KVEF 160000
AFDVEF

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Las Vegas NV
311 PM PST Sun Nov 15 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Next chance for rainfall, breezy conditions, and cooler weather 
  Monday evening through Tuesday 

* Winter Storm Watch issued for the Eastern Sierra Wednesday morning 
  through Friday morning for accumulating snow

&&

.DISCUSSION...Through Saturday

Much calmer and drier conditions continue across the region today as 
brief ridging is in place for the next 24 hours. Satellite imagery 
this afternoon shows mainly clear skies over the Desert Southwest 
with high clouds from the next incoming trough streaming in from the 
Pacific into Central California and Nevada. Current LAS ACARS 
soundings reveals the dry airmass near the surface and increasing 
moisture above 400mb. Overall expect mainly clear skies for the rest 
of today then increasing clouds on Monday as deeper moisture and 
clouds advect in with the southwesterly flow ahead of the trough. 
Trends in the guidance over the past 24 hours have really slowed 
down this next system and associated precipitation; therefore expect 
a mainly dry day for Monday as well despite increasing clouds. 

By Monday evening, deep troughing pushes inland along the California 
Coast with a 100 kt SSW jet out ahead of it and a 40-50 kt LLJ 
developing overhead, ahead of the trough axis. ECMWF ensemble mean 
PW is still around 0.80-0.90" extending as far north as Lincoln, 
Nye, and Inyo counties. Strong LLJ support and modest low and mid 
level lapse rates of 6-7 C/Km may result in periods of moderate to 
heavy rainfall under the strongest showers. However a lack of any 
surface based or elevated CAPE will keep the severe threat near zero 
and the thunder and lightning threat fairly low. While there is good 
low and mid level southerly flow advecting moisture northward, 
enough downsloping may be occuring to keep the best chance for 
measurable rainfall outside of the Las vegas Valley. QPF for Las 
Vegas valley remains low ranging from nothing to up to a tenth of an 
inch while REFS PPM indicate up to almost an inch portions of 
Lincoln County and over a half inch for higher elevations in Mohave, 
San Bern, eastern Nye County. Showers begin to develop around sunset 
Monday evening across the region then become more widespread 
overnight with the low level jet support. With latest trends slowing 
down the overall system, expect showers to persist for Lincoln, 
Clark, and Mohave Counties through at least Tuesday morning and 
early afternoon, drying out from west to east. Again, greatest 
coverage of rainfall and showers looks to be across Nye, Lincoln, 
and Mohave Counties and higher terrain Monday night with more 
scattered showers likely over Clark County. Not very concerned with 
snow at higher elevations as any amounts in the Sierra should remain 
under warning criteria and snow levels do not fall until most of the 
moisture has exited the region for the rest of the Lower Great Basin 
and Mojave Desert.

Watching for a period of breezy conditions to develop as the trough 
axis swings through Tuesday morning and afternoon. Cold air 
advection steepens low and mid level lapse rates allowing winds from 
the low and mid level jet to mix to the ground. Latest ECMWF 
Ensembles show strong agreement for a period of wind gusts of 30-40 
mph on Tuesday, with locally higher gusts possible in wind prone 
areas such as around Barstow and Daggett. A Wind Advisory may be 
needed in future forecast issuances for wind prone areas as 
confidence increases. 

Expect a brief period of dry conditions late Tuesday into Wednesday 
for most of the area; however the next system to impact the region 
will be right on the heals of the previous one. Focus now shifts to 
the heavy snow potential in the Sierra beginning as early as 
Wednesday morning. WPC ensemble cluster analysis shows great 
agreement among models and ensembles and are largely in phase 
regarding the amplified upper level pattern. Clusters show strong 
consensus on a deep trough digging into the West Coast, directing an 
atmospheric river with the Sierra. NBM snow accumulation 
probabilities for higher elevations of the Sierra have been 
consistently going up the past several days. While model spread does 
begin to increase Friday onward, there is enough forecast confidence 
already to issue a Winter Storm Watch for the Eastern Sierra Slopes 
above 5,000 feet elevation where 1-3+ feet of snow could fall. The 
watch goes from Wednesday morning to Friday morning. Since this is 
still several days away, expect some changes to the forecast; 
however confidence is increasing for heavy accumulating snow for the 
Eastern Sierra. Elsewhere across the Lower Great Basin and Mojave 
Desert, troughing will keep cooler temperatures in place as well as 
the chance for showers Thursday and early Friday. There is still 
quite a bit of spread in QPF amounts across the region; so 
confidence remains lower in impacts outside of the Sierra for the 
Thursday-Friday timeframe. However confidence does remain high in 
another round of rain and showers for the region; lower confidence 
exists in exact amounts and overall system evolution as it pushes 
east of the Sierra. 


&&

.AVIATION...For Harry Reid...For the 18Z Forecast Package...Light 
easterly winds become variable this evening, followed by westerly 
winds overnight. Cloud cover gradually increases and cloud bases 
lower throughout the forecast period. FEW to SCT clouds with bases 
of 6-8kft move in overnight. Coverage increases to SCT to BKN at 4-
7kft tomorrow morning. Showers may develop within the vicinity of 
the terminal by tomorrow afternoon.

For the rest of southern Nevada, northwest Arizona and southeast
California...For the 18Z Forecast Package...Light winds with periods 
of variability can be expected for most locations throughout the TAF 
period. One exception is the northern Owens Valley including KBIH, 
where gusty southerly winds pick up late this morning, lasting into 
the evening. Peak gusts should be in the 20 to 25 knot range. Cloud 
cover will increase and cloud bases will lower, with bases between 7 
and 10kft by tomorrow morning. 

&&

.SPOTTER INFORMATION STATEMENT...Spotters are encouraged to report
any significant weather or impacts according to standard operating
procedures.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Moore
AVIATION...Meltzer

For more forecast information...see us on our webpage:
https://weather.gov/lasvegas or follow us on Facebook and Twitter
